label: NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB (Volta) — CloudLab c4130 (Wisconsin)
statements: Measured ceilings: memory bandwidth 845 GB/s (94% of the datasheet 900 GB/s); GEMM 7.0 TFLOP/s fp64, 14.1 TFLOP/s fp32. Every percentage below is relative to these measured ceilings.
Bandwidth-bound workloads at their largest size reach B1 SAXPY 100%; B2 LBM D3Q19 95–96%; B3 SpMV (CSR) 9–78%; B4 SpGEMM (CSR) 2–9% of measured bandwidth.
Compute-bound workloads with a FLOP model reach C1 GEMM 96–99%; C3 2D Convolution 11–27% of the measured GEMM peak.
Llama-3 inference (llama3.2-1b): decode B=1 at 71% of measured bandwidth; decode B=8 at 60% of measured bandwidth; prefill at 103% of measured GEMM peak.

Fastest implementation where several were timed — A1: PyTorch + CUDA graph fastest on 2/2 sizes (PyTorch at 0.44× median); C3: native kernel fastest on 18/18 sizes (PyTorch at 0.42× median); S1: torch.histc fastest on 15/18 sizes (torch.bincount at 0.66× median); S2: CUDA graph launch fastest on 4/4 sizes (cooperative launch at 0.90× median).
Clocks were not locked: the median clock during the largest GEMM was 1,392 MHz (recorded in every row as freq_mhz).

Data: 522 validated rows from 3 process-isolated trials (commits 09d3e54, 2999f37, 3b1a3f2); 36 unsupported (unsupported:bf16 not native on this device); 117 skipped because the working set exceeds device memory; 0 errors; 8 rows flagged unstable (CV > 5%).

findings.title: Llama decode measures the memory system only after two fixes
findings.text: Generating one token at a time should be limited by reading the weights. Two harness problems hid that: (1) PyTorch's fused attention kernel tiles over query tokens, so with one query most of each tile was idle (47% of the step at batch 1, 64% at batch 8), and (2) each step issues ~500 small kernels from Python, which this node's 2016 Xeon could not launch as fast as the GPU ran them. Decode attention is now two batched matmuls over an in-place KV cache, and decode is also timed replayed from a CUDA graph (as serving engines run it). llama3.2-1b fp32: batch 1 66.8 → 117.6 tokens/s, batch 8 251 → 678.5 tokens/s.

findings.title: Clock speed explains the GEMM gap to the datasheet
findings.text: GEMM reached 14.1 TFLOP/s fp32 against a 15.7 datasheet figure. The datasheet assumes the 1530 MHz boost clock; under its 300 W power limit this GPU ran GEMM at ~1392 MHz (15.34 × 1392/1520 = 14.05 matches the September legacy run, which held 1520 MHz). Clocks are recorded, not locked. Because the ceiling is measured at whatever clock that GEMM ran at, a kernel that ran faster can exceed it slightly: Llama prefill ran at ~1493 MHz and shows 103% of the measured GEMM peak.

findings.title: Small problems can beat the memory ceiling
findings.text: Sizes whose data fits in the 6 MB L2 cache are not limited by HBM bandwidth (SAXPY n=1M: 1,010 GB/s vs the 845 GB/s ceiling). The ceiling markers are drawn only for problems that stream from device memory.

findings.title: Irregular sparse workloads sit far below the bandwidth line
findings.text: SpMV on a regular 3-D Poisson matrix reaches 78% of bandwidth, but on a power-law matrix only 9%, and SpGEMM 2–9%: random gathers and the symbolic phase (inside the timer, by design) waste most of each memory transaction. These are cuSPARSE results as measured; the 'bandwidth-bound' label does not hold for them.

findings.title: What the 16 GB Volta card cannot run
findings.text: Volta has no bf16 hardware, so every bf16 row is recorded 'unsupported' instead of emulated. Problems are skipped before running when 2.5× their working set exceeds ~14 GB of usable memory: Llama-3.2-3B and Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.2-1B decode at batch 32, SAXPY n=1G, LBM n=512 and AES on 4 GB. The 2.5× safety margin is conservative; some of the 8–9 GB problems would probably fit (open item).

findings.title: SHA-256 may be below well-tuned GPU code
findings.text: The custom CUDA SHA-256 reaches 52–105 GB/s. Each thread reads its own message, so loads are not coalesced; a layout that interleaves messages may be much faster. To confirm: profile with Nsight Compute (memory throughput vs instruction throughput) before using C9 in a CPU-GPU ratio.
